import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Zariski Cancellation

*Reference:* [arxiv/2208.14736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14736)
**The Zariski Cancellation Problem and related problems in Affine Algebraic Geometry**
by *Neena Gupta*
-/

namespace Arxiv.«2208.14736»

open Polynomial

/--
A finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` is cancellative if for all finitely generated `k` algebras `B` such that
`B[X] ≅ₖ A[X]` we have `B ≅ₖ A`.
-/
def IsCancellative (k A : Type*) [Field k]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] : Prop := ∀ {B : Type*}
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra.FiniteType k B], Nonempty (A[X] ≃ₐ[k] B[X]) →
    Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[k] B)

/--
The **Zariski Cancellation Problem**: every polynomial ring over a field `k` of characteristic
`0` is cancellative.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem {k : Type*} [Field k]
    [CharZero k] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] : IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial ι k) := by
  sorry

/--
The single variable polynomial ring `k[X]` is cancellative in any characteristic
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.dim_one
    {k : Type*} [Field k] : IsCancellative k k[X] := by
  sorry

/--
The two variable polynomial ring `k[X]` is cancellative in any characteristic
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.dim_two {k : Type*} [Field k] :
    IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) := by
  sorry

/--
The positive characteristic case of the Zariski Cancellation Problem is false in dimension `3`
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.false_pos_card
    (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (hι : Fintype.card ι = 3) :
    ¬ IsCancellative (ZMod p) (MvPolynomial ι (ZMod p)) := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«2208.14736»

findings.description: The docstring at line 58 calls `k[X]` the two-variable polynomial ring. Here `k[X]` denotes the univariate ring `Polynomial k`. The theorem itself correctly uses `MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k`, so only the documentation is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: Gupta, arXiv:2208.14736, Section 2 following Question 1′, discusses the affirmative result for n = 2 and explicitly calls it the cancellation property of k[X,Y]. https://arxiv.org/e-print/2208.14736
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `k[X]` in this docstring with `k[X, Y]` or `MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k`; leave the theorem statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The survey quantifies over arbitrary k-algebras B, whereas Lean explicitly assumes `Algebra.FiniteType k B`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since A is finitely generated over k, A[X] is finitely generated. An isomorphism A[X] ≃ₐ[k] B[X] transfers finite generation to B[X]. Evaluation at zero is a surjective k-algebra homomorphism B[X] → B, so B is automatically finitely generated. Thus the added hypothesis does not restrict the relevant B. The exact equivalence is proved as `cancellation_iff_source` in /workspace/review/complete.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses arbitrary finite variable-index types, including the empty type, while Question 1′ uses a positive integer n and the premise B[X] ≅ₖ k[X₁,…,Xₙ₊₁].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Reindexing by `Fintype.equivFin` identifies the indexed polynomial ring with the ring in n variables. `MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv` identifies its polynomial cylinder with the ring in n+1 variables, and algebra isomorphisms can be reversed. The extra n = 0 case is true: from k[T] ≅ₖ B[Y], evaluation at Y = 0 makes B an algebraic quotient of k[T]; the embedding B → k[T] then has constant image, forcing B ≅ₖ k. Both this boundary result and the full equivalence with the survey’s positive-n formulation are proved in /workspace/review/complete.lean (`field_cancellation` and `main_iff_source_positive`).
